div.div: The same vision encoder sits well above the Orin's ridge (compute-bound: the compute form is right) but near Thor's effective ridge, where neither form alone is safe (illustrative encoder, sibling ceilings)
arithmetic intensity (FLOP per byte of DRAM traffic), log scale

vision encoder, weight side
500 FLOP/B [vision_encoder: intensity_flop_per_byte, illustrative]
Thor DRAM 197.3 GB/s, sustained by a pi0.5-class VLA [pi05_sustained_bandwidth_thor]
Vision time: the two forms of the prediction vs an illustrative measurement (ms; 0.5 TFLOP, weights about 1 GB, my estimate from `vision_encoder`)
Thor rows: my estimates from `vision_encoder`, `pi05_sustained_bandwidth_thor`, `tensor_fp16_thor` and `shape_rate_fraction`. No Thor vision time is given here.

Orin: the form was what mattered. Intensity ÷ ridge is about 2.1 at the roof, 3.5–5.2 at the shapes, so the encoder is compute-bound and the compute form brackets the measurement. The bandwidth form misses by about 4.2 times (my estimate from `vision_measured_ms_orin` and `vision_pred_bandwidth_form_ms`): the wrong form, not a slow encoder.

Thor: the data do not decide. Intensity ÷ ridge is about 0.51 at the roof, 0.85–1.28 at the shapes: the two forms give about the same time, so either roof could bind. Thor's compute roof is about 4.5× the Orin's, its bandwidth only about 1.1× (my estimate from the four sibling keys).

Caveats. The weight-side intensity is an upper bound for one pass; counting all DRAM traffic lowers it and moves the encoder toward the ridge on both boards. The shape-rate fraction is illustrative and applied to Thor by assumption. Thor's bandwidth is a sustained value from a VLA, not a read peak: with Thor's read peak (259 GB/s [dram_read_thor]) the ridge is about 743 FLOP/B (my estimate from `tensor_fp16_thor` and `dram_read_thor`), about 3× the Orin's roof ridge rather than about 4×; the encoder stays near it. Axes are approximate; the labelled values are exact.

Legend
blue solid = Orin roofs; orange dash-dot = Thor roofs
shaded dotted bands = GEMM rate at the model's own shapes
purple dashed = the encoder's weight-side intensity
right: dashed outline = the first prediction; black line = measurement
bars under the plot = ridge at shapes; tick = at the roof

Sources. Note B4. Roofline and ridge: ../../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/ (glossary, note C1). Ridges, weights and Thor times are my arithmetic.
Illustrative (round teaching numbers that keep the shape of a finding; not measurements): vision_encoder, shape_rate_fraction, vision_pred_bandwidth_form_ms, vision_compute_form_ms, vision_measured_ms_orin.
Sibling (keys in a sibling public kit; paths relative to the kit folder): tensor_fp16_thor = ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/constants.json tensor_tcgen05_fp16.thor; tensor_fp16_orin = ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/constants.json tensor_classic_fp16.orin; dram_read_orin = ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/constants.json dram_bandwidth_read_measured.orin; pi05_sustained_bandwidth_thor = ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/constants.json pi05_sustained_bandwidth; dram_read_thor = ../jetson-orin-thor-metrics/constants.json dram_bandwidth_read_measured.thor.
